comparisons.peer_topic: Consolidated Balance Sheet Liabilities and Composition Changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Total liabilities were $1.55 trillion as of December 2024, an increase of $29.29 billion from December 2023, primarily driven by increases in collateralized financings and deposits, partially offset by decreases in customer and other payables and borrowings.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose changes in their consolidated balance sheet liabilities, specifically highlighting movements in payables and deposits. JPMorgan reports a decrease in 'Accounts payable and other liabilities', attributing it to timing in Payments and lower client payables in Markets. In contrast, Goldman Sachs reports an overall increase in total liabilities, driven by collateralized financings and deposits, but notes a specific decrease in 'customer and other payables' which reflects client activities, serving as a comparable line-item discussion on the dynamics of payables within the balance sheet composition.

sentences.text: Accounts payable and other liabilities decreased primarily driven by lower payables in Payments related to the timing of processing payment activities, due to December 31, 2023 falling on a weekend, as well as lower client payables related to client-driven activities in Markets, partially offset by the impact of the adoption of updates to the Accounting for Investments in Tax Credit Structures guidance effective January 1, 2024.

As of December 2024, total liabilities in our consolidated balance sheets were $1.55 trillion, an increase of $29.29 billion from December 2023, primarily reflecting increases in collateralized financings of $35.03 billion (reflecting the impact of our and our clients' activities), and deposits of $4.60 billion (due to an increase in consumer deposits, partially offset by decreases in transaction banking deposits and other deposits), partially offset by decreases in customer and other payables of $7.47 billion (primarily reflecting our clients' activities) and borrowings of $5.48 billion (driven by net maturities).
